text:
maria-c: quick follow-up from the postmortem — i sketched a lean plan for adding the tests we promised (regression catalog + prompt sets + a couple load scenarios). listing owners + sprint commitments here so we can track in one place

maria-c: goals: 1) curate a regression catalog of triggered cases, 2) add prioritized prompt sets for regressions, 3) add 2 load tests (burst and steady), 4) schedule 1 chaos drill focused on model fallback policies

maria-c: ownership suggestions: tj -> regression catalog curation; kelsey -> prompt sets + eval harness; samir -> load tests & infra; olivia -> chaos drill coordination + runbook updates

kelsey: ok with that. i can start by pulling the postmortem examples and canonicalizing prompts. estimate 3 days to get an initial ~20-prompt set and 1 week to integrate into ci-evals pipeline

tj: i'll take the catalog. plan: tag each item with incident id, affected route, SLO impact, repro steps, and suggested test type. will add a tiny metadata schema in the repo so it's searchable

samir: load tests: i'll prototype a k6 script for the steady and a short 5min burst harness. need a dedicated perf namespace; can we get 2 gpus in staging for the bursts?

olivia: chaos drill — i'd like to run the first one in two weeks, target a single route, validate fallback to smaller quantized model + latency SLO. will produce a runbook draft by monday

maria-c: timeline proposal (please ack or push back): sprint A (next week): tj catalog initial 30 items + kelsey initial prompts (M-W). mid-sprint: samir prototype load scripts. sprint B: CI integration + chaos drill prep. final sign-off sprint C: dry-run chaos + merge into main. owner action items to be added to the postmortem ticket

tj: ack. will put the first PR up by Wed with schema + 15 items

kelsey: ack. monday i'll add the prompt formatting rules (meta: expected output, tolerance, token budget). also want to add one example eval harness snippet:```yaml
name: run-regression-evals
on: ubuntu-latest
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v3
  - run: make run-evals SUITE=regression/incident-sets
```

samir: +1 on perf namespace. ct team, can we get staging-gpu-2 for 3 days during sprint A? tagging infra here but posting in eng-infra channel as well

olivia: ack timeline. for the chaos drill i'll draft failure modes: 1) KV cache thrash, 2) model OOM, 3) region failover. will attach measurable success criteria (latency/throughput/recovery window)

maria-c: notes on acceptance: each new test must be runnable in CI with clear pass/fail, have a short doc blurb, and be stored under /tests/regression-catalog/<incident-id> with metadata.json including owner and priority

kelsey: question — how do we label 'flaky but expected' vs 'regression'? propose a field severity:{must-fix, tolerable, info}. that way alerting can map to pager or ticket creation

tj: good call. we'll include severity and a reproducibility score (1-5). also add 'trigger' boolean for tests that should run on every deploy vs nightly

samir: for load tests i'll add a tags field so they can be picked by the perf job. sample k6 command: `k6 run --vus 200 --duration 5m script.js` — we'll wrap that in the perf runner

olivia: planning note: i'll coordinate with support to include a few recent customer reports as part of the prompt set so we test real world phrasing

deploy-bot: reminder: link to the postmortem ticket -> https://issues.redwood.example/PM-4123 added as thread reference

maria-c: next steps: i'll create an umbrella tracking ticket and add sub-tasks for each owner with the timelines above. please add acceptance criteria to your subtask by EOD tomorrow. i'll do a quick sync on Wed 10am to confirm sprint A priorities

tj: i'll update my subtask tonight

kelsey: will add acceptance criteria + example outputs

samir: will request staging quota today

olivia: will draft the chaos runbook and invite SRE + oncall for the dry-run

maria-c: thanks all — this is actionable enough. marking as in-progress. :thumbsup:
